The series **converges**. Wolfram|Alpha's result page for `sum from n=1 to infinity of 1/(n^3+1)` loaded with "Sum convergence: Show tests" and "Infinite sum: More digits" pods. I read those pod labels from the page text, but the pod contents are images, so I did not read the convergence verdict or the numeric value off the page.

The convergence follows from the limit comparison test with 1/n³: the limit of (1/(n³+1)) / (1/n³) as n→∞ is 1, which is positive and finite, and Σ 1/n³ converges (p-series with p = 3 > 1).

I also estimated the value by summing the first 10 terms (≈ 0.6820) and adding an integral tail bound (≈ 0.0045), which gives roughly 0.6865. That is my own estimate, not a value from Wolfram|Alpha.
